To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the GaN on Si (111) technology has a potential for power devices with a higher performance than the GaN on silicon (100).
the use of Si(1 11) substrate for the growth of GaN high electron mobility transitors (HEMTs) is an attractive option for monolithic integration with Si MOSFETs in the millimeter-wave range.
GaN on (1 1 0) silicon is a good candidate for monolithic integration with Si-MOSFETs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of high performance transistors on Si(1 1 0) for the realization of compact power amplifiers in millimeter-wave and terahertz range.
the development of GaN-based transistors for millimeter-wave and high-power applications, with a special emphasis on the use of Si(1 11) substrates.
the integration of GaN on silicon substrates for microwave power electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GaN-based power transistors on Si(1 1 0) substrates have the best potential for integration with Si-based technologies.
the Si(1 1 0) substrate is a promising alternative to the more expensive SiC substrate for the fabrication of GaN-based power transistors.
the (1 0) and the (1 2 0) substrates are not suitable for GaN-on-silicon power devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GaN-on-Si(1 1 0) technology is very promising for power electronics at frequencies up to 40 GHz.
the Si(1 1 0) substrate is more suitable than Si(1 0 0) for GaN-based devices.
the (1 0 0) and (11 0) orientations are both suitable for the realization of GaN-based devices on silicon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GaN on silicon is a very interesting material platform for monolithic integration of high-power devices.
the (1 0 0) orientation of silicon substrates does not provide the expected advantages for GaN-based high-power transistors.
the use of Si(1 11 0) substrates is a promising way to improve the performances of GaN-based power transistors and to make more compact microwave power electronic circuits.
